newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Air transport said underpinning global economy.
newsitem.headline: Air transport said underpinning global economy.

text.p: The jobs of a total of 24 million people around the globe were dependent on the air transport industry in 1994, two million more than in 1992, a Geneva-based aviation body reported on Monday.

The Air Transport Action Group (ATAG) -- which links airlines, airports, aircraft manufacturers, tourist bodies, labour union, business and consumer groups -- issued the figures in its latest monthly bulletin.
It said the total economic impact of air transport on the world economy in 1994 was $1,140 billion, compared with $1,000 billion in 1992.
By the year 2010, ATAG said, that figure could exceed $1,700 billion and the industry could be underpinning over 30 million jobs.

"These new figures confirm the growing economic importance of air transport to the world, and the continuing need for capacity improvements to adequately cope with forecast growth," the bulletin declared.
The figures were released as the International Air Transport Association (IATA), the global airlines body which helped form ATAG in 1990, was opening its annual general meeting in Geneva.
ATAG defines itself as an independent coalition of organisations, formed to press for economically beneficial aviation capacity improvements "in an environmentally responsible manner."
